description: Proposes changes to an EXISTING mind map: add branches, rename a node, write a note, tick a task, remove a branch, illustrate a node, put a screenshot on a node (op "img" with `file`) — or, with op "persona", re-cast a WORK MAP canvas from a finished interview (the JSON block of the « ma cartographie du travail » skill). Nothing is applied — the proposal appears in TabTree as a banner on that map, the user reviews it change by change and picks what to keep (and can undo with Cmd+Z afterwards). Name each target node by its exact text, or by a path "Ancestor > Node" when the same wording appears twice. Read the map first so the wording matches.

changes.description: The proposed changes, applied in order

assign.description: assign: a name or e-mail ("" clears it). add: optional — the owner of the NEW cards. When read_map shows a 👥 Team, pick from it, by role, what each person owns and their objectives

col.description: move: the kanban column id (read_map shows them), or "" to take the card off the board. add: optional — the column the NEW cards go to

data.description: img: a data:image/…;base64 URL instead of `file`

due.description: due: the due day as YYYY-MM-DD ("" removes it)

est.description: est: the estimate as a duration — "2h", "1h30", "45" (minutes), "2:15" — or "" to remove it

file.description: img: full path of the screenshot (PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF) on this machine. It is re-encoded to about 840 px and becomes the node's cover picture.

img.description: img: pass "" to REMOVE the screenshot from that node (otherwise give `file` or `data`)

markdown.description: add: the new branch as a bullet list, 2 spaces per level

note.description: note: the note body (empty string clears it)

op.description: add = new children under `target`; rename = change its text; note = set its note; check = tick/untick the task; delete = remove it and its children; move = send the card to a kanban column; pic = put an illustration on it; img = put a SCREENSHOT on it (give `file`, the path of the image on this machine — or `data`; `img: ""` removes it); persona = re-cast a work map canvas (a board whose name starts with “Work map —” / “Cartographie —”) or a Second Brain Blueprint (“Second brain —”) from an interview — no target; tags = set the card's colour labels; assign = who the task is for; priority = 1 (highest) to 6; due = the due day; attr = set a “Name: value” attribute on the node (an estimate, a budget…); comment = add a signed comment to the card's thread (give `text`); est = set the time ESTIMATE of the task (give `est`, e.g. "2h", "45" = 45 minutes, "" removes it)

persona.description: persona: the interview object exactly as the skill returns it — who, role, mission, tools, meetings, opener, modules[{name, procs[{name,h,after,freq,rep,data,stakes,lever,step,why}]}], trajectory, signs, parking. TabTree rebuilds the canvas AND its companion sheet from it.

pic.description: pic: "a:<id>" for a built-in illustration, or "e:<emoji>" for one large emoji, or "" to remove it. Ids: person, team, chat, idea, target, trophy, star, heart, warning, done, flag, clock, laptop, phone, mail, folder, book, chart, money, calendar, building, car, globe, rocket, house, pin, plane, coffee, plant, sun, camera, music, lock, key, health, gift.

priority.description: priority: 1 (highest) to 6, or 0 to remove it

tags.description: tags: the colour labels to set, from: green, yellow, orange, red, purple, blue, sky, lime, pink, gray — read_map shows the name the board gave each colour. [] clears them.

target.description: Exact node text, or "Ancestor > Node" if ambiguous (not used by persona)

text.description: rename: the new text. comment: the comment body (plain text; http/mailto links become clickable)

value.description: attr: its value, e.g. "2h" ("" removes the attribute)

why.description: Any change: optional — one short line saying WHY (e.g. "Owns the website"). Shown to the user next to the change, so they can judge it

file.description: The map to change — a file name (or map name) from list_maps

note.description: One line telling the user what this proposal does and why. Shown above the changes.

name: propose_changes
